newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: EU expects 85% of countries to sign infotech pact.
newsitem.headline: EU expects 85% of countries to sign infotech pact.

text.p: The European Union (EU) said on Thursday it expects 85 percent of countries covered by an agreement to scrap tariffs in global information technology markets to sign the agreement by Friday.

"I expect that countries representing around 85 percent of world trade will be willing to sign on tomorrow," Peter Carl, European Union chief negotiator on the Information Technology Agreement (ITA), told a news conference in Singapore.
The agreement was hammered out in lengthy negotiations between the EU and the United States this week at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting here.
EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said earlier that the pact would become final if countries representing about 90 percent of world trade in the sector sign it by March 15, 1997.
"The EU is already confident that by March 15 the 90 percent target is likely to be achieved," the EU said in a statement distributed at the news conference.
The statement said the ITA met 98 percent of the EU's original negotiating objectives in terms of volume of trade.

The deal would cover capacitors (energy-storing devices used in computers), digital photocopiers, fibre optics cables, computer monitors, telecoms equipment, computer software and semiconductors. It would exclude graphic display tubes.
Tariff cuts would take place in four stages up until January 1, 2000, at the latest, and beginning in July 1997, subject to agreed exceptions, it said. -- WTO newsroom (65 3376070)
